title: The Old Man and His Grandson
text:
There was once a very old man whose eyes had grown dim, whose ears were dull and whose knees trembled. When he sat at the table he could hardly hold his spoon. He spilled soup on the tablecloth, and some of it ran out of his mouth.

His son and his son's wife were disgusted. They made him sit in the corner behind the stove and gave him his food in an earthenware bowl, and not even enough of it. He sat there looking at the table with tears in his eyes.

One day his trembling hands could not hold the bowl, and it fell and broke. The young wife scolded him. He said nothing but only sighed. They bought him a wooden bowl for a few coins, and he had to eat from that.

Some time later the parents saw their little son, four years old, sitting on the floor gathering bits of wood together. "What are you doing?" his father asked. "I am making a little trough," the child answered, "for Father and Mother to eat out of when I am big."

The man and his wife looked at each other and began to cry. They brought the old grandfather back to the table at once, and from then on he always ate with them, and they said nothing if he spilled a little.
lesson: Children are watching how we treat our parents, and they are learning how to treat us. Patience with the old is also a lesson for the young.
people: An old grandfather, his son and daughter-in-law, their child
source: Brothers Grimm, Kinder- und Hausmarchen, No. 78 (Der alte Grossvater und der Enkel)
